pellicula.notes: Every row of jacks follows one rule: a mono jack overrides its voice, a polyphonic jack drives by channel any voice whose mono jack is empty, and with neither patched the knob stands. The sample jack is a pitch jack in shape but a chooser in effect: it is quantised to semitones and a semitone is one sample on. The playback engine is a clean-room reimplementation of the Erica Synths Pico DRUM sample player, built from the published manual with no code from the hardware or any port. imber.notes: The five clocks and eight effects are not placed by hand: each object owns two rolled positions and the two morph knobs glide the whole population between them, which is the one deliberate departure from the original's mouse canvas. Divisions and effect kinds never change, only positions. The field display is a custom widget rather than a control, so no click in it reaches this help; a muted player is drawn there as a hollow ring rather than a filled dot. Mute, volume and the engine switch are all exempt from Rack's randomize and from the module's own randomize button, because they are performance state rather than sound design. Loop windows drunk-walk in steps of 200ms up to the maximum loop length, and samples come from a bank of 64 by an urn, so the same one never comes twice in a row. The module is inspired by Giorgio Sancristoforo's Haiku: the architecture, timing model, effect designs and voice behaviour follow a reverse-engineering of it, while the generator's numbers were tuned by ear. The sylla module plays the same generated library as a standalone voice. The panel prints imber, x, y, chg, new, clk, fx, rch, cpl, cv, bpm, spd, lpm, skp, sks, scv, rvl, vol, rnd, pls, inst, plv, div, bit, nse, tap, on, seed, rr clk, nd clk, rr fx, nd fx, trg, clr, xcv, ycv, 2n, 4n, 8n, 16n, 32n, skip, micro, L and R.

viginti.notes: The model is the published state-space system of the circuit from Danish, Bilbao and Ducceschi's DAFx20in21 paper, section 3.1, with the component values from Stinchcombe's 2006 study of the MS10 and MS20 filters and the diode nonlinearity solved through the Lambert W function. The resonance knob is exponential in Q from 0.5 to 50 over its first 85 per cent and covers the self-oscillating stretch over the rest. Self-oscillation is started by a deliberate noise floor of about 8 microvolts at the circuit's input, because the ideal model at rest would sit at zero forever. The output is inverted, as the circuit is. configBypass passes the audio input to the output. This is the low-pass section only; the MS-20's highpass is a different circuit and is not modelled. The panel prints viginti, cutoff, res, fm, drive, level, res, v/oct, fm, in and out.

materiae.notes: The two oscillators are naive squares with no band limiting, and the module's character comes from how they are read rather than from what they are. The ratio table holds nineteen entries: 1:2, 2:3, 3:4, 5:4, 4:3, 3:2, 5:3, 7:4, 2:1, 5:2, 3:1, 4:1, a unison, a unison detuned by one per cent, the square root of two, e, pi, and a 1:4 at the bottom; the menu can swap the knob for a free sweep from a quarter to four times. artifex.notes: The time knob has two CV jacks sharing one attenuverter: one continuous and one sampled and held on each step of the clock. The mode and rhythm CV jacks both span their whole list over ten volts and wrap, so an oscillator sweeps the machine without trimming; a small attenuverter setting picks between two neighbouring modes instead. Mode changes from CV wait for the next clock step by default, so a modulated change lands on the beat. The two pattern switches are each normalled to the jack below them. The euclidean half of the rhythm list skips six densities because at sixteen steps those are patterns the hand-written half already holds. The module is built after Bastl Instruments' Citadel FX Wizard, and its bottom half is the same circuit as vates's. vates.notes: The bank is stepped by two buttons rather than swept by a knob, as on the hardware, where only the samples sit under a knob; both displays can be right-clicked for the whole list. The sample knob spans its bank end to end, so its top is the last sample rather than the first again; the wrapping belongs to modulation. On the hardware, play and cue are the sign of one attenuverter, which means play mode can never be modulated downward; splitting the mode onto its own switch lets the attenuverter run the full range in either mode. The length knob does the envelope and the direction together, and at either end the envelope is held open, so on the longer generated banks a sequence becomes a drone rather than a run of hits. The kits folder is shared with pellicula. The module is built after Bastl Instruments' Citadel, and its bottom half is the same circuit as artifex's.
